original_question: Given a planar figure, or more generally a body in space, and a distance d > 0, what is the largest possible size of a set of points contained in that region such that the distance between any two chosen points is at least d?
target_in_paper: Numbered problem 149, “Maximum points,” on p. 78: the paper asks for the maximum number of points contained in a given planar figure, or more generally in a space body, whose pairwise distances are at least a prescribed d>0. This is the closest official formulation to your draft. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the essential content of problem 149 very closely: it fixes a region, introduces a separation threshold d>0, and asks for the largest cardinality of a point set in that region with mutual distances bounded below by d. It also correctly stays with the point-set version, rather than drifting to the nearby but different circle/sphere inclusion problem (145) or the covering-style minimum-point problem (150). ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
missing_details: The paper poses the question for a fixed given planar figure (and, in the stated generalization, a fixed space body), not as an optimization over all figures or all bodies. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
The parameter is stated explicitly first: d is a real number with d>0. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
The scope is exactly planar figure first, then “generally: in a space body”; the paper does not formulate this item in arbitrary dimension n. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

To make the question fully stand-alone, one should spell out that the distance is the ordinary Euclidean distance between distinct points of the figure/body; this is implicit in the paper’s geometric wording. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

The precise quantifier structure is: maximize |S| over subsets S of the given region such that for all distinct x,y in S one has |x-y|≥d. Your draft conveys this informally but not in fully explicit mathematical form. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))

The paper does not ask for an algorithm, asymptotic estimate, or a reformulation in terms of circles or spheres; those belong to nearby but different numbered problems. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
refined_question: For a fixed planar figure F in the Euclidean plane—or, in the paper’s stated generalization, for a fixed body B in Euclidean 3-space—and for a real number d>0, determine the maximum possible cardinality of a subset S⊂F (respectively S⊂B) such that |x-y|≥d for every pair of distinct points x,y∈S. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
justification: The paper is a compilation of numbered sequences, questions, conjectures, and unsolved problems, and your draft aligns almost verbatim with item 149 rather than with a broader neighboring topic. The nearby context matters: item 145 asks about packing circles/spheres in a region, while item 150 asks the distinct dual-style question of the minimum number of points needed so that every point of the region lies within distance d of one of them. Hence the sharp paper-faithful refinement is the item-149 maximum-cardinality point-separation problem and not a broader packing or covering variant. ([fs.unm.edu](https://fs.unm.edu/Sequences-book.pdf))
